chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام asking him about one who has fallen unconscious for a day or more: should he make up what he missed of the salat (prayer), or not? So he wrote: He does not make up the sawm (fasting), nor does he make up the salat (prayer).

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ عَلَيْهِ السّ: Imam Abu al-Hasan the Third عليه السلام, to whom the legal question was addressed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the obligatory salat (prayer) missed during the period mentioned
key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: the obligatory sawm (fasting) missed during the period mentioned
key_terms.الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: a person who has fallen unconscious
key_terms.يَقْضِي: to make up a missed religious duty

ai.seo_question: Does a person who was unconscious have to make up missed prayers and fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question addressed to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام concerning a person who was unconscious for a day or more. The Imam عليه السلام replies that such a person does not make up either the missed sawm (fasting) or the missed salat (prayer), making it a concise ruling on acts of worship missed during unconsciousness.
